name: Checking a Contractor’s License in California
headline: Checking a Contractor’s License in California
articleBody: In California, a kitchen renovating contractor should generally hold an active contractor’s license for the appropriate trade classification before performing contracted work that exceeds the state’s threshold for licensed contracting. The Contractors State License Board explains that consumers can verify a license, check bonding and workers’ compensation status, and review disciplinary history through its license lookup system. For kitchen projects, this matters because the work often blends multiple trades such as carpentry, plumbing, electrical, drywall, and tile, and the contractor must be authorized to contract for the scope being offered. Homeowners should also confirm that the legal business name on the estimate matches the license record, because a recognizable brand name does not always mean the contracting entity is the same as the licensed entity. In addition, California requires contractors to provide a written contract for home improvement work over a certain dollar amount, which helps tie the licensed party to the agreed scope and payment terms. In practice, a consumer in Los Angeles County should compare the license record, proof of insurance, and the exact entity name on the bid before signing. This is one of the strongest ways to reduce risk before a remodel begins.
